name: snmalloc-rs (snmalloc global allocator)
verdict_reason: snmalloc's claim that frees on another thread do not slow it down holds: in an independent 2026 mimalloc-bench run it was the fastest allocator on the cross-thread xmalloc test, 7.2x faster than glibc and 25x faster than jemalloc. On real programs it beat glibc by 4% to 18%, in line with mimalloc.
tier_reason: A third-party mimalloc-bench run with public scripts and raw CSV, CPU, OS, glibc version and -march=native stated.
claimed_speedup: mimalloc-bench, snmalloc 0.7.4 vs glibc 2.43: xmalloc-testN 0.102 vs 0.739, sh8benchN 00.25 vs 01.19, leanN 0:07.66 vs 0:09.05, espresso 0:02.85 vs 0:03.23, redis 0:2.160 vs 0:2.240; jemalloc took 2.573 on xmalloc-testN.
workload: mimalloc-bench allt suite: real programs (espresso, lean, redis) and multithreaded stress tests, including xmalloc-test, where one set of threads allocates and another frees.
hardware: Intel Core i7-13800H, 14 cores / 20 threads, 30 GiB RAM
platforms: Linux and BSDs (ELF platforms named in the README) and other targets snmalloc supports; default build needs CMake and a C++ compiler
one_liner: Rust bindings for Microsoft's message-passing allocator; 7.2x faster than glibc on cross-thread frees and 4-18% faster on real programs.
how_it_is_fast: Memory freed by its allocating thread needs no synchronization. Memory freed by another thread is batched into messages and returned to the owning allocator's queue, so thousands of remote frees cost one atomic operation. The malloc fast path is two branches on Linux when compiled with Clang.
use_it_when: Producer-consumer pipelines where one thread allocates and another frees (channels, work queues)
Many-core servers with heavy cross-thread object hand-off
skip_it_when: Memory-tight deployments: on xmalloc-testN it peaked at 158908 KB vs glibc's 59672 KB
Builds that cannot depend on CMake and a C++ toolchain
caveats: mimalloc-bench runs C and C++ programs, not Rust, built with -march=native on one laptop CPU.
The benchmark used snmalloc 0.7.4; the current snmalloc-rs crate is 0.7.6.
The crate moved from SchrodingerZhu/snmalloc-rs (now archived) into the snmalloc repository.
tradeoffs: Higher peak memory on some stress tests (larsonN: 244528 KB vs glibc's 175144 KB).

evidence.quote: Allocations on one thread are freed by a different thread
Both of these can cause massive reductions in performance of other allocators, but do not for snmalloc.
13th Gen Intel Core i7-13800H, 14 cores / 20 threads
